patch.value: Re-anchoring overwrites the original hash pair, so the immutability proof for every pre-merge entry is destroyed by the operation that repairs the chain

pm-w7ccmv states the outcome as every mutation immutably recorded, independently verifiable, restorable to any version. The first two clauses hold for a stream that has never been merged and stop holding the moment one is.

reanchorHistoryEntries in src/core/history/replay.ts:321-390 replays a stream from an empty document, recomputes beforeHash and afterHash at each step, and writes the rewritten entry as {...entry, patch: outPatch, before_hash: beforeHash, after_hash: afterHash} at lines 365-370. The entry's original before_hash and after_hash are overwritten in place and are not retained anywhere: the returned ReanchorResult carries an entriesRehashed count and a per-entry ReanchorEntryDetail whose rehashed field is a boolean. So the operation records THAT a hash changed and never records what it was.

Re-anchoring is not an exceptional path. src/sdk/merge/three-way.ts:57 documents the reanchored flag as 'true for every union merge', and a union is the normal outcome whenever two branches both appended to the same stream - which is the ordinary case for concurrent agents, and the case the merge fence exists to serve. docs/MERGE_SAFETY.md describes the history driver as preserving both divergent suffixes, ordering deterministically, then re-anchoring, and the driver emits guidance to run pm validate --check-history-drift and pm history-repair afterwards. All of that is sound as chain repair. None of it preserves the prior anchors.

The consequence is specific and worth stating precisely, because the chain does still verify. After a merge, a verifier can confirm that the merged sequence is internally consistent: each entry's before_hash equals the replay hash of its predecessors. What a verifier can no longer do is confirm that any given entry was originally written against the state its author observed, because the value the author committed to has been replaced by a value derived from the merged ordering. An entry altered during the merge window - by a faulty driver, a bad conflict resolution, or deliberate tampering - produces a merged stream that verifies exactly as cleanly as an honest one. The property that makes a hash chain evidence rather than a checksum is that the anchors are fixed at write time by a party who did not know the future; re-anchoring replaces them with values computed after the fact.

A second, narrower loss sits in the same function. When a patch does not apply strictly, the lenient path at lines 346-356 recomputes the stored patch as jsonPatch.compare(replay, next) and counts skippedOps. Operations the original author recorded can therefore be absent from the rewritten patch, with only an aggregate count surviving. The recorded intent is replaced by a diff of outcomes.

This is adjacent to but not covered by what already exists. pm-9j2r3b closed by making merged state replay-addressable through receipt-backed merge_reconcile events, which solves addressability of the merged result and not provenance of the inputs. pm-85hm delivered the audited history-repair command. pm-lwmstb owns receipt settlement after repair. pm-34w8za owns deduplicating the load-verify-rewrite-re-anchor pipeline across redact, repair and compact - and that consolidation is the natural place to add retention once, since all three paths re-anchor.

Scope is retention and verifiability, not preventing re-anchoring, which is necessary and correct. The original anchor pair for every rewritten entry needs a durable home - alongside the entry, in the merge receipt, or in a checkpoint - such that a third party holding the pre-merge streams and the post-merge stream can confirm that re-anchoring changed only anchors and ordering and changed no author, timestamp, operation or patch content. The same requirement applies to redaction and compaction, which re-anchor for their own reasons, and history compaction additionally prunes prefixes, so the retention design has to survive pruning or explicitly record what it can no longer prove.

The original before_hash and after_hash of every re-anchored entry are retained durably, so a verifier can reconstruct the pre-re-anchor anchor set without holding the pre-merge stream; A verification path confirms that a re-anchor changed only anchors and entry ordering, and did not change any author, timestamp, operation, message or patch content, and fails loudly when it did; The lenient patch-repair path records the original patch operations it replaced or skipped, not only an aggregate skippedOps count, so recorded intent survives a repair; The same retention applies to every path that re-anchors - merge, history-repair, history-redact and history-compact - enforced once at the shared pipeline rather than per command, which makes pm-34w8za a natural carrier; History compaction states explicitly what it can no longer prove after pruning a checkpointed prefix, so the loss is recorded rather than silent; A negative-control test tampers with one entry's author or patch inside a simulated merge window and proves the verification path rejects the resulting stream, since a check that cannot fail adds no assurance
After a union merge, a third party can independently verify that the merge preserved every recorded mutation and altered only anchors and ordering.

The original anchors are overwritten in place and retained nowhere; the merged chain verifies identically whether or not entry content was altered during the merge, and a lenient patch repair can replace recorded operations with a diff of outcomes while retaining only a count.

value.text: A hash chain that is repaired by recomputation stops being tamper evidence and becomes a checksum. The distinguishing property is that anchors are fixed at write time by a party who cannot see the future; once any maintenance path recomputes them, an altered stream and an honest one verify identically. Every re-anchoring operation therefore needs to retain what it replaced, or the guarantee it protects is only as strong as trust in the operation itself.
